subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The recruitment process usually begins with:
options: Identifying a vacancy and producing a job description
questions.explain: Recruitment starts by identifying a vacancy and writing a job description and person specification.

questions.q: Herzberg argued that factors such as pay and working conditions are:
options: The only thing that motivates employees
Hygiene factors that prevent dissatisfaction but do not strongly motivate
questions.explain: In Herzberg's theory, hygiene factors like pay and conditions stop dissatisfaction but do not actively motivate.

questions.q: An advantage of internal recruitment is that:
options: The candidate is already known to the business and it is usually cheaper
It avoids the need for training
It always brings in fresh ideas from outside
It guarantees a larger pool of applicants
questions.explain: Internal recruitment is cheaper and the applicant is already known, though it may limit fresh ideas.

questions.q: A financial method of motivation is:
questions.explain: A bonus is a financial reward, so it is a financial method of motivation.

questions.q: Delayering an organisation means:
options: Removing one or more layers of management from the hierarchy
questions.explain: Delayering removes layers of management, widening spans of control and shortening the chain of command.

questions.q: In an organisational structure, the 'span of control' is:
options: The length of the working day
The number of employees a manager is directly responsible for
The number of layers in the hierarchy
questions.explain: Span of control is the number of subordinates a manager directly supervises.

questions.q: Why is effective communication important within a business?
options: It removes the need for managers
It ensures instructions and information are understood, reducing errors
questions.explain: Good communication ensures information is passed clearly, reducing mistakes and improving coordination and motivation.

questions.q: According to Maslow, which is a lower-level (basic) need?
options: Physiological needs such as pay for food and shelter
questions.explain: In Maslow's hierarchy, physiological needs (e.g. basic pay) are at the bottom and must be met first.

questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial method of motivation?
questions.explain: Job rotation and added responsibility motivate without extra pay, so they are non-financial methods.

questions.q: The chain of command refers to:
options: The line of authority through which instructions pass down the organisation
questions.explain: The chain of command is the line along which orders and authority pass from top to bottom.

questions.q: On-the-job training means:
options: Watching online videos at home only
Learning while doing the actual job at the workplace
questions.explain: On-the-job training takes place at the workplace while the employee carries out the job.

questions.q: A delegated task is one where a manager:
options: Passes authority for a task down to a subordinate
questions.explain: Delegation is when a manager passes responsibility and authority for a task to a more junior employee.

questions.q: An autocratic leadership style is one where the leader:
options: Always consults the whole workforce first
Lets employees make all the decisions
Makes decisions alone and tells staff what to do
questions.explain: An autocratic leader makes decisions without consulting staff and expects instructions to be followed.

questions.q: Taylor's theory of motivation suggests workers are mainly motivated by:
options: Money and pay linked to output
questions.explain: Taylor argued workers are chiefly motivated by money, e.g. through piece-rate pay linked to output.

questions.q: A democratic leadership style involves:
options: The leader making all decisions alone
The leader involving employees in decision-making
questions.explain: A democratic leader consults and involves employees when making decisions.

questions.q: Job enrichment as a motivation method involves:
options: Giving an employee more challenging and meaningful tasks
questions.explain: Job enrichment adds more challenging, meaningful work and responsibility to motivate employees beyond pay.

questions.q: A laissez-faire leadership style means the leader:
options: Gives employees a high degree of freedom to make their own decisions
questions.explain: A laissez-faire leader gives employees freedom and minimal direction, leaving them to make their own decisions.

questions.q: Off-the-job training takes place:
options: Only while doing the actual job
After an employee has left the business
Away from the normal work position, e.g. at a college or training centre
During the employee's lunch break only
questions.explain: Off-the-job training happens away from the workplace, such as on a course at a college or training provider.

questions.q: An advantage of external recruitment is that it:
options: Brings in new skills and fresh ideas from outside the business
Guarantees the candidate already knows the firm
Means no training is ever needed
Is always cheaper than internal recruitment
questions.explain: External recruitment can bring in new skills, experience and fresh ideas that the existing workforce may lack.

questions.q: Why is staff retention important to a business?
options: Keeping experienced staff reduces recruitment and training costs
Retention has no effect on costs
questions.explain: Retaining experienced staff lowers the cost of recruiting and training replacements and keeps knowledge in the firm.

questions.q: A decentralised structure can benefit a business because:
options: Head office controls every small choice
Local managers can make quicker decisions suited to local needs
No one is given any authority
questions.explain: Decentralisation passes decision-making to local managers, allowing faster decisions tailored to local conditions.

questions.q: A 'tall' organisational structure has:
options: Many layers of hierarchy and narrow spans of control
questions.explain: A tall structure has many hierarchical layers, usually with narrow spans of control.
